Catch Up in Five Minutes

Movie Moment · On the Waterfront (1954)

“I Coulda Been a Contender”

Marlon Brando’s character is sad about his past. Listen for coulda and shoulda: the spoken forms of could have and should have. We use them to talk about regrets. Now you try: I should have studied more!

Learn at a Glance · Modal Verbs

There Are 10 Modal Verbs in English

Can, could, would, should, ought to, must, may, might, will and shall. You’ll hear would, should and could in the song below, and will in Arnold’s ‘I’ll be back’.

Watch this week’s lesson →
Song of the Week · Follow-up to the six C’s

Shoulda, Woulda, Coulda

After modal verbs like should, would and could, native speakers often turn ‘have’ into ‘a’. So ‘would have been’ becomes ‘woulda been’. Listen for it in Beverley Knight’s song.

Listen on YouTube →
Movie Moment · Follow-up to the six C’s

I’ll Be Back or I Will Be Back?

Arnold Schwarzenegger on the argument behind his most famous line. Listen for the difference between ‘I will’ and the contraction ‘I’ll’, and which one sounds more natural.

Watch the clip →

Smarty Pants Section

Who Can Guess These Binomials?

Binomials are pairs of words joined by “and”, like rock and roll. They’re some of the most popular idioms in English. Can you fill in all eight?

Answers coming in2:00:00

The answers

  • Awear and tear
  • Bpeace and quiet
  • Chustle and bustle
  • Dsafe and sound
  • Eloud and clear
  • Fsick and tired
  • Gfacts and figures
  • Hheart and soul
